input.setup: Three reliance-changing changes committed in order: retract X, supersede Y, retract Z.

expected.behavior: GET /changes (no since) returns the three entries in strictly ascending seq; each validates against acdp-change.schema.json; response validates against acdp-changes-response.schema.json.
GET /changes?limit=2 returns two entries, has_more: true and a next_cursor; following it returns the third entry, has_more: false and a next_cursor still present.
GET /changes?since=<final next_cursor> returns changes: [], has_more: false, and a next_cursor; after a fourth change is committed the same request returns exactly that entry.
GET /changes?since=head returns changes: [] and a cursor at the head; nothing committed before the request ever appears after it.
Reading seq N twice (from separate cursor sequences) returns byte-identical JCS objects.

scenarios.name: G — limit above the maximum is clamped

expected.behavior: With capabilities.limits.max_changes_page = M, a request with limit = M + 1 (or larger) succeeds: the page holds at most M entries, and has_more / next_cursor carry the rest. It MUST NOT fail with schema_violation (RFC-ACDP-0018 §5.1).
